paragraphs: The 220i has been part of the 2 Series range since 2014. Early F22/F23 models (up to 2016) use the N20 — a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine. From 2016 onwards, the 220i switched to the B48, a newer generation of the same capacity. The current G42 generation continues with the B48. The key difference between the two is their reliability profile: the N20 has a documented timing chain issue on earlier cars, while the B48 is generally considered a more robust design.
about.boldParagraph: The 220i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol fitted to the 220i from 2014 to 2016. Known for timing chain guide failure on early cars — a well-documented pattern shared with the 1 Series and 3 Series of the same era. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N20 rebuild.

A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol fitted to the 220i from 2016 onwards. This is the later, more reliable replacement for the N20 — generally well-regarded with fewer documented issues. We service it to the same standard as our other 220i rebuilds.
The current 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol fitted to the G42-generation 220i. This is the same B48 engine family as the later F22/F23 cars, with the same reliability profile.

compatibility.intro: The 220i spans two distinct engine families across three generations. The early N20 (pre-2016) has its own specific wear points — particularly the timing chain and guides. The later B48 (2016 onwards) is a different unit with its own components and service requirements. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:
